frequency_question: How often does a submitted nuclear cooperation agreement get blocked by a joint resolution of disapproval enacted into law?
membership_rule: Includes any peaceful nuclear cooperation agreement formally submitted to Congress for the statutory review period; excludes informal drafts or unsubmitted executive understandings.
provenance_note: claims 40 cases from only 6 named (6.7x); beyond 3.0x the skeleton is not carrying the estimate
coverage_note: Over forty agreements submitted historically; zero instances of successful legislative blocking via joint resolution.
known_gaps: Minor technical amendments or dormant agreements omitted from detailed public logs, but none resulted in enacted joint resolutions of disapproval.
skeleton: Legislative review periods for Section 123 agreements since the Atomic Energy Act of 1954, totaling roughly 40+ submitted agreements, zero of which have been successfully blocked by a joint resolution of disapproval enacted over a presidential veto.
validity_reason: Statutory framework under the Atomic Energy Act for congressional review of nuclear agreements remains structurally stable over decades.
